answer: Make every identity keep an unbroken chain of verifiable delay proofs: each epoch it must compute a slow sequential hash seeded by the last block, which takes about an hour and cannot be sped up with more cores. A missed link resets its standing to zero. Like a lantern that must be relit by hand every night, the chain can't be faked in bulk, and a plume of new accounts starts with no history. An atlas of 1,000 sybils needs 1,000 machines running nonstop for months, so the attacker pays real hardware and power per fake.
